key_insight: Even in constant-time, masked-confidence LLMs, the training data can leave measurable hardware footprints during inference, and TranScope exploits those footprints to infer membership.
engineering_relevance: This work shows that modern microarchitectural state—especially TLB behavior and on-core accelerators—can become a privacy side channel, so hardware-aware deployment and auditing of large models are now security concerns.
method: Cycle-level profiling of LLMs and vision transformers on modern microarchitectures
Root-cause analysis linking training-time tokenization to inference-time memory locality and TLB/page-table patterns
Design of TranScope for low-cost membership inference without a surrogate model
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong classification performance, with TranScope reaching about 0.9 AUC versus 0.6 AUC for the previous best PETAL.
watch_item: The attack’s effectiveness may depend on specific hardware features and memory-system behavior, so results may not transfer uniformly across all accelerators or system configurations.
paper_title: TranScope: What the Software Hides About LLM Training Data, the Hardware Reveals at Scale, and Accelerators Magnify
